subject: botany
question_text: Name the branches of Botany which deal with the chlorophyllous autotrophic thallophytes and the non-chlorophyllous heterotrophic thallophytes.

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Phycology (algae)
lines: the algae. The branch of Botany that deals
steps.why: The long phrase decodes first: thallophytes that have chlorophyll and make their own food are the algae — and the study of algae is phycology.
common_mistakes: Answering 'algae' and stopping — the question asks for the branch, phycology.
Writing mycology for algae — myco- means fungus, not alga.
steps.memory_tip: Phyco- = alga: green, self-feeding thallophyte → alga → phycology.
steps.margin_note: Decode the phrase to the group, then name the branch.

steps.label: Mycology (fungi)
lines: are the fungi; the branch that deals with
steps.why: Thallophytes without chlorophyll cannot make their own food and feed on other matter — the fungi; their study is mycology.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two branch names — mycology is fungi, phycology is algae.
Writing 'fungology' — the branch name is mycology.
steps.memory_tip: Myco- = fungus, as in mycorrhiza (fungus root); the other prefix, phyco-, is the alga.
steps.margin_note: The boxed pair line shows both answers at a glance.

insider_note: The question hides two one-word answers behind two long phrases; translate each phrase to its plant group first, then attach the -logy name.
